transcript:
User: Oh I LOVE this. Yes. Absolutely. ...Wait, what were we saying? Sorry, yes, go on!
Agent: Haha, I love your energy too — no worries at all.  

So, to ground us: are you mainly trying to stop losing customers from missed calls, or are you more focused on getting more leads booked in your calendar?
User: Oh, both sound just fantastic! Yes! Let's do whatever you think will help best! I'm all in!
Agent: Got it, I love the enthusiasm — sounds like you really want to tighten things up.  

So today, when someone calls your business and no one can pick up right away, what usually happens to that call?
User: Oh, that's such a great question! Usually, it just goes to voicemail, you know? But I'm open to suggestions!
Agent: Gotcha, so most of them just land in voicemail.  

Do people actually leave messages for you, or do you feel like a lot of those callers just hang up and move on to the next business?
User: Oh, totally! Sometimes they leave messages, sometimes not. Whatever works is good! It's all so exciting, right?
Agent: Haha, you’re fun — and yeah, it *is* pretty exciting when you can actually catch all those people.  

Mhm, so those calls that *don’t* leave a message and just disappear… what worries you most about that — lost revenue, missed opportunities, or just the general chaos of not knowing who tried to call?
User: Oh, definitely the mystery! Isn't it thrilling? But also, yes, missed opportunities. Let's catch them all somehow!
Agent: Love how you put that — “the mystery” is exactly it.  

So roughly, how many calls a week would you say end up in that mystery zone where they hit voicemail and you never really hear from them?
User: Oh, quite a few, I'd say! But you know, it's hard to keep track. Just loads of them, really!
Agent: Got it — “loads” and no real way to track them totally fits what I’m hearing.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those mystery missed calls might be costing you in real dollars each month, or has it mostly just been a gut feeling so far?
User: Oh, mostly a gut feeling, yes! But I'd love to know more about the real dollar impact. Sounds amazing!
Agent: Makes sense — most folks run on gut here until they actually see the numbers.  

So ballpark, if you had to guess, how many calls a week hit voicemail and never really turn into anything — are we talking more like 10, 30, 50+?
User: Oh, I love numbers! Let's say 30, but could be 10. Or more! Whatever feels right to you!
Agent: Gotcha, let’s run with 30 for now and we can always adjust.  

And of those 30 missed calls, what percent do you feel would’ve actually booked with you if someone had picked up — maybe around 40–60%, or something else?
User: Oh, absolutely, 50% sounds fantastic! Or maybe 45%? Really, whatever you think feels right is good!
Agent: Nice, let’s keep it simple and use 50% — easy math.  

Last one: on average, what’s a call worth to you when it *does* turn into business — more like $200, $500, $1,000 a job, or somewhere in between?
User: Oh, somewhere in between! I'd say $500 sounds amazing, but maybe $1,000? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Perfect, let’s keep it at $500 so we’re not overhyping anything.  

So… given all that, it’d be really useful to actually walk through how we stop that mystery bucket and what your numbers look like with this turned on — would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough sometime this week to see it?
User: Absolutely, that sounds amazing! Hmm, maybe Tuesday? Or Wednesday? Whatever you think works best! Can't wait!
Agent: Love it, I can hear you’re all in.  

First thing so I don’t lose you — what’s your first name?
User: Absolutely! It’s Wendy! Yes, just Wendy. So excited to be doing this! Let’s keep going!
Agent: Got it Wendy, I’m excited too.  

And what’s your last name?
User: Oh, it's Marsh! Like a marshmallow, you know? Isn't that fun? Excited to keep this going!
Agent: Haha, Marsh like marshmallow is great, I love that.  

So, what’s the name of your company?
User: Oh, thanks! It’s just Wendy’s thing, you know? W-Marsh Consulting? Whatever you think fits best! So exciting!
Agent: Love the excitement, Wendy.  

So for this week, would you rather do Tuesday or Wednesday for that walk‑through?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Hmm, actually Tuesday's bad... oh wait, is it Wednesday? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Gotcha, sounds like Tuesday might be messy, so let’s roll with Wednesday.  

On Wednesday, I can get you in as soon as 11:00 or 11:45 Eastern — which of those feels better for you?
User: Oh, both sound wonderful! Yes! Hmm, maybe 11:00? Or 11:45? Whatever you think is best! Exciting!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Wendy, you’re all set for Wednesday at 11:00 Eastern with Jay. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation and a link to add it to your calendar or reschedule if you need to. Before I let you go, is there anything else you need from me right now?
